question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` plus `defaultAccount`, root configuration as the implicit default account, and one messaging listener per named bot as its durable public contract?
rationale: The PR creates permanent configuration, credential, routing, listener, setup, and stored-state semantics that correctness review and green checks cannot authorize by themselves.

options.title: Sponsor and reopen
options.body: Accept the proposed accounts/defaultAccount model, preserve root config as the implicit default, and reopen or adopt the implementation for landing.

options.title: Sponsor a revised contract
options.body: Retain the account-aware runtime work but revise listener deployment or shared-setting inheritance before reopening.

options.title: Do not sponsor
options.body: Leave the PR closed and keep the canonical issue available only if maintainers later choose a different Teams multi-account direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and reopen
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed accounts/defaultAccount model, preserve root config as the implicit default, and reopen or adopt the implementation for landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows the broadest ownership of Teams lifecycle, state, setup, and plugin architecture affected by this contract.
